nodes.description: Cultured human podocytes with ARHGDIA siRNA or mutant overexpression (Gee), and mouse podocytes with shRNA knockdown alone or reconstituted with each patient allele (Gupta; Auguste).

The constitutive null developed massive proteinuria and died of renal failure within a year, with tubular degeneration and dilatation; males were infertile. A later study in the same line showed increased renal Rac1 (not RhoA) and mineralocorticoid receptor signalling, reduced by a Rac inhibitor, and suppression of albuminuria by mineralocorticoid receptor blockade.

Homozygous germline ARHGDIA variants in five families: a nonsense allele (p.Arg120Ter), missense alleles (p.Gly173Val, p.Gly168Arg), an in-frame single-residue deletion at the GTPase-binding interface (p.Asp185del) and a canonical splice-acceptor variant (c.275-1G>A). The in-frame deletion and the nonsense allele abolish binding of RhoGDIalpha to its GTPases; G173V retains partial binding in one study but still fails to restrain RAC1, which is the proposed basis for its later onset.

Loss of RhoGDIalpha disturbs podocyte actin and motility, but the direction of the motility change depends on the experimental system: overexpression of mutant alleles over endogenous wild-type protein, or siRNA knockdown, enhanced migration of human podocytes, whereas replacing endogenous RhoGDIalpha with the mutant forms slowed mouse podocytes, reduced actin polymerization and cell size, and increased cellular projections. The studies agree that podocytes are sensitive to the balance of Rho-GTPase activity.
